title.narrative: Immediate life-saving support to people living with HIV/AIDS affected by flooding and mudslide in Fr

description.narrative: From initial assessment conducted by NETHIPS, SWAASL and SLYDD, approximately 100 Households (HHs) of people living with HIV/AIDS from different communities in the greater Freetown area, are affected by both flooding and/or mudslide. Among those affected by the disaster, people living with HIV/AIDS (PLHIV) are particularly vulnerable and require specific attention to consistent availability of food, hygiene and protection information, provision of dignity kits as well as eventual support through cash transfer. While being highly vulnerable, these identified households are not currently consistently supported by humanitarian actors. There is an urgent need to immediately address the needs of these households, as lack of nutrition, risk of waterborne/water-related diseases, protection concerns, and lack of hygiene information and materials are likely to have a severe impact on health and well-being of these households.
